lesson.menu_desc: Telling the story with the setback in it, and what the date does to the verb -- 33 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 3 -- Past vs. Now
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Andreia Naim Finianos | Lesson 3 -- Past vs. Now

listenings.text: The version of this story people like is the one where we signed the partnership agreement and everything worked. That is not the story. We signed it in March and by June the whole thing had almost fallen through, because the people who agreed to it were not the people who had to live with it. Our contact left, the new one backed out of half of what we had agreed, and for about eight weeks I genuinely thought we had lost the year. What turned it around was boring. We followed up. Every week, same day, same short message, no pressure, for two months. Eventually somebody on their side said, look, nobody has been this patient with us, let us start again. We have signed four agreements since then and I have run every single one the same way. I learned that the hard way and I would not have believed it if somebody had told me.

I joined in the middle of an acquisition, which is not a thing anybody should do on purpose. My first week was a room full of people who had been told nothing and a system that two companies were using in two different ways. I hit the ground running because there was no other option, and honestly I made a lot of mistakes in that first month. The breakthrough, if you can call it that, came from a conversation in a corridor. Somebody from the other side told me what everybody was actually afraid of, which was not the software at all. It was the reporting line. We changed the plan that week. I have worked on three integrations since then and the first question I ask now is never technical. It has been the same question every time: what is the thing nobody has said out loud yet?
